answer: Use a proof-of-work-over-time delay on registration. A new key must compute a sequential hash chain, a verifiable delay function, for seven days, then submit the output, which any verifier checks in milliseconds. Parallel hardware cannot shorten sequential steps, so each identity needs its own dedicated core for a full week. Like a quill bound to one hand, one core serves one key. Reaching a wharf of market access, then nectar rewards, costs a farm of one thousand fakes roughly one thousand core-weeks, about five dollars each.
